title: Northstar Check-in: All-Hands Micro-Playbook (Aug 2026)
content:
Purpose and context:

This micro-playbook is a compact, action-focused plan to prepare the company for an August 2026 All-Hands that centers on a short "Northstar Check-in" and an exec update on capacity, risk, and the next quarter's OKR framing. The goal is to create a tight, repeatable format that highlights decisions and asks rather than long presentations. Treat this file as the single source for run-of-show, owners, and comms artifacts while the more polished deck and speaker notes are produced.

Why a micro-playbook: we have observed meeting fatigue from long town halls and a need for clearer follow-through. This version prioritizes: 1) decisions and clear asks, 2) a short executive arc (3 min founder framing, 6 min product/metrics, 6 min ops/availability, 6 min go-to-market), 3) 10-15 min open Q&A with pre-gathered questions and fast followups.

High-level objectives for the All-Hands (draft OKRs / outcomes we want):

- Outcome A: Shared clarity on "what we will protect" for the next 90 days (latency SLOs, Dedicated capacity commitments, Private pipeline).
- Outcome B: Alignment on top 3 company-level OKR drafts and their 30-day war-rooms (owners assigned).
- Outcome C: Reduce cross-team friction by announcing 2 new operational guardrails (release freeze window + a model fallback policy).
- Outcome D: Surface 5 specific asks of engineering and product leaders (one-line each) with delivery checkpoints.

Draft Company-level OKRs (short lines, owner, and 30-day hook):

1) OKR: Make inference latency predictable under 95% of load spikes
   - Owner: Raj Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
   - Key results (draft): Reduce  p95 response time for cold-start requests by 30%; Create a canary path for model fallbacks for the top 10% traffic flows.
   - 30-day hook: Canary rollout plan and two emergency rollback playbooks published.

2) OKR: Lower per-token cost for the top 5 customers by 20%
   - Owner: Maya Alvarez (product-hosted-api)
   - Key results (draft): Autoscaling + smarter batching configs applied to top 5 flows; Publish per-route cost dashboards.
   - 30-day hook: Cost-reduction experiment plan and KPI dashboard link shared with CS.

3) OKR: Harden Private deployment onboarding and security attestation
   - Owner: Simone Dubois (security-and-compliance)
   - Key results (draft): VPC deployment playbook, KMS integration test, and one pilot customer onboarded.
   - 30-day hook: Pilot kickoff and compliance checklist signoff.

Run-of-show (compact):

- 00:00–03:00 — Founder framing (northstar + what we will protect). Leah to give 3 crisp bullet points.
- 03:00–09:00 — Product + metrics highlight (Maya): top customer wins, per-route costs snapshot, quality regressions (if any).
- 09:00–15:00 — Serving runtime / infra health (Raj): capacity table, major incident status, SLO posture.
- 15:00–21:00 — Security & Private deployment update (Simone): pilot status, compliance asks.
- 21:00–28:00 — GTM and adoption (Connor): sales signals, top 3 support asks for product teams.
- 28:00–40:00 — Live Q&A (moderated). Pre-gathered top 6 questions will be used first, then open mic.
- 40:00–45:00 — Closing + 3 measurable asks and immediate next steps.

Speakers & prep checklist (who does what):

- Leah Kim (owner of this doc): final run-of-show, confirm slide 0 (3 bullets), record leader notes. Due: Aug 3.
- Raj Patel: compile capacity snapshot and p95/p99 charts, link to dedicated capacity commit table. Due: Aug 5.
- Maya Alvarez: customer highlights + cost dashboard export (CSV) and a 1-slide summary of product tradeoffs. Due: Aug 5.
- Simone Dubois: compliance pilot status and 1-slide summary of remaining blockers and mitigation plan. Due: Aug 6.
- Connor O'Brien: GTM ask list and 2 minute adoption pitch. Due: Aug 5.
- Comms lead (TBD): draft all-hands invite copy, highlight 3 asks in subject line, gather internal pre-questions. Due: Aug 7.

Pre-gathered Q&A process:

- Collect questions via a short Google Form linked in Slack (channel #all-hands-questions). Closing time: 24 hours before event.
- Moderator (Leah) will triage top 6 questions and route any technical deep-dives to follow-up sessions.

Comms timeline (quick):

- T-7 days: Save-the-date and ask for 1 pre-question (Slack + calendar).
- T-4 days: speaker slide checklist and one-paragraph exec summary.
- T-2 days: final deck, run-of-show, and rehearse with speakers (10–15 min run).
- Day-of: 30-min speaker arrival, check recording, Slack live thread open.

Decision anchors (what to decide at the meeting):

- Approve the three company-level OKR drafts and their owners (quick yes/no poll).
- Approve a release freeze window for the next 14 days surrounding the Dedicated capacity migration (yes/no).
- Approve automatic fallback policy for highest-risk models (owner Raj to publish implementation plan).

Risks and mitigations (short list):

- Risk: Data-quality or model regressions discovered during demo -> Mitigation: Demo uses sanitized, pre-evaluated prompts and has fallback notes in speaker deck.
- Risk: Overrun Q&A and poor time control -> Mitigation: Moderator enforces timebox; follow-up office hours scheduled.
- Risk: Confusion on who owns follow-ups -> Mitigation: Publish decision log within 24 hours with owners & deadlines.

Immediate next actions (this doc is the canonical to-do until we cut the deck):

1) Leah: Confirm speaker list and finalize run-of-show (Due Aug 3).
2) Raj: Upload capacity snapshot CSV to the linked artifact and add 2 annotated charts (Due Aug 5).
3) Maya: Export cost dashboard and provide one slide with recommended batching/quantization headline (Due Aug 5).
4) Simone: Share compliance checklist and pilot timeline (Due Aug 6).
5) Comms: Draft invite + Google Form for pre-questions and post the T-7 announcement (Due Aug 2).

Follow-up cadence after All-Hands:

- +24 hours: Publish recording, decision log, and owners list.
- +7 days: Short status update from each OKR owner on progress (1 paragraph).
- +30 days: War-room checkpoint and adjustment of KR targets if needed.

Appendix A — Quick Q&A templates for speakers (use as copy/paste):

Q: What does this mean for my team's sprint?
A: Short answer (15s) + owner + where to find the detail (link). Example: "No immediate freeze on feature work; teams touching Dedicated capacity should coordinate with Raj. See playbook: [link]."

Q: How will we measure cost improvements?
A: We will use per-route cost dashboards and a top-5 customer cohort comparison; Maya will publish the baseline numbers in the next 48 hours.

Appendix B — Runway/Staffing heatmap (summary):

- Weeks 0–4: Focused on deploying canary and compliance pilot. Resource pull: Eng-serving-runtime core + SRE tilt.
- Weeks 4–8: Customer onboarding for Private pilot and follow-up cost experiments.

Notes and freeform signoffs: please add comments inline in this doc. If you are listed as an owner, add your short 1-line readiness note below your name and update the due date if it slips.

End of micro-playbook.
